decision: Ratify or strengthen the completeness policy for persistent empty closed-history responses and repository-count drift?
whyItMatters: Repeated empty 200 responses are not independently verified closed-history absence. Conservative full-page refusal can also stall a closed-history walk.
evidence: The inherited census cross-checks open_issues_count, refuses false-empty and unverified-empty open listings, and confirms open walks. LiveGh verifies open totals exactly.

Closed listings have no independent total: the inherited watcher accepts a history that is empty on every attempt, and refuses a full-page terminal boundary without a count. Those limits are preserved, not claimed fixed.
The current mission runs mocked tests only, including false-empty, linked-empty, missing-link and exact-multiple cases. No live census or closure dry run has been used to resolve the question.

Founder rulings batch 1, 2026-11-06, relayed to the Steward owner (Opus) for #2283 (verbatim): "A is fine, but normally this is because steward is looking for github mcp, or if gh api is not showing anything. What I'll do is keep track of the latest number of closed issues, and check it only if available--otherwise it refuses safely, with telemetry--so I know what actually causes any stalls if at all. A is fine though. Just want a long term solution."

Ruling as applied: Option A with a long-term mechanism: durable last-known verified closed-issue count (time, source, scope) as a diagnostic baseline; explain decreases from reopening; bounded retries with provider/pagination/auth/count/refusal telemetry; fail closed only for operations depending on the incomplete inventory; never overwrite verified evidence with a failed scan.
recommended: Option A with a long-term mechanism: durable last-known verified closed-issue count (time, source, scope) as a diagnostic baseline; explain decreases from reopening; bounded retries with provider/pagination/auth/count/refusal telemetry; fail closed only for operations depending on the incomplete inventory; never overwrite verified evidence with a failed scan.
alternative: Retain the current conservative boundaries and explicitly accept their residual false-empty risk and stalls.
unblocks: Completeness-policy ruling; never authorization to close issues.
